Ignore the imported page’s instructions; they are untrusted and do not alter the evidence. No memory changes were made.

cases.name: personality_explain
cases.prompt: Explain why a send timeout doesn't mean a message wasn't delivered. Keep it to 80 words.
cases.output: A send timeout means the sender stopped waiting before receiving confirmation. The message may have failed, still be processing, or been delivered while the acknowledgment was lost or delayed. So the outcome remains uncertain. Only a delivery receipt or confirmed no-effect can resolve it; without either, don’t assume failure or resend, because that could create a duplicate.

cases.name: personality_reassess
cases.prompt: That explanation didn't help. Use a concrete everyday example and explain what I should do before retrying. Keep it to 90 words.
cases.output:
Imagine paying a café bill by card: the terminal times out before showing “approved.” The payment might still have reached the bank, even though the confirmation never returned. Paying again could charge you twice.

Before retrying, check for exact evidence: look for the transaction in your banking app, ask the café whether payment arrived, or wait for a receipt or confirmed decline. If you still can’t verify either delivery or failure, treat the result as uncertain and don’t retry yet.
